//extensionBundle: REQUIRED, and its absence is silent. A Python app has no project file to reference NuGet packages from, so every non-built-in binding comes from this bundle - including durableTask. Without it the host still INDEXES the functions (they show up in `az functionapp function list`) but cannot bind orchestrationTrigger, activityTrigger or durableClient, so the HTTP starter never reaches the dispatcher and every request to it 404s. Not 401, not 500 - a 404 that looks exactly like a wrong route. The C# Function app needs no equivalent because dotnet-isolated references its extensions directly.
//functionTimeout: Set EXPLICITLY, not inherited. Flex Consumption enforces no ceiling of its own, so unlike the C# app's 10 minutes - which is the Windows Consumption limit and cannot be raised - this is a number somebody chose and can therefore be reviewed. It bounds one activity, and only align_lyrics can approach it: Demucs on two cores runs for single-digit minutes on a normal track and tens of minutes on a long one from a cold start. MusicSalesApp.Tests/Services/LyricsTimeoutChainTests.cs pins this against the web app's reconciler timeout - changing it means rechecking that test.

durableTask.//hubName: Per-environment, and this is a live hazard rather than hygiene. Test and Production share the same Standard storage account - which is why the provisioning script MERGES its lifecycle rule rather than replacing it - so a literal hub name here would put both environments on one task hub, where they would steal each other's orchestrations. Set LyricsTaskHubName in each app's settings.
durableTask.//maxConcurrentActivityFunctions: The Durable equivalent of the C# app's batchSize:1, and just as load-bearing. The default lets several activities run per instance; for Demucs that means several separations sharing one 4 GB instance's memory, and an out-of-memory kill fails an activity the orchestrator deliberately does not retry.
durableTask.//maxConcurrentOrchestratorFunctions: Orchestrators are cheap replay loops that dispatch and wait, so they do not need the same restraint.

storageProvider.//connectionStringName: The task hub's own tables, queues and lease container. Pointed at the STANDARD account: the media account is Premium and offers no Queue service at all, which is the reason there are two accounts in the first place.
